newsitem.title: INDIA: India SBI share falls after Euroissue.
newsitem.headline: India SBI share falls after Euroissue.

text.p: The share of State Bank of India (SBI), the country's largest commercial bank, fell on Bombay bourses in early trade on Friday after it completed an issue of global depositary receipts (GDRs), brokers said.
The share fell 3.5 rupees, or 1.46 percent, to 235.50 at the Bombay Stock Exchange.
It was down 4.30 rupees, or 1.79 percent, at 235.85 on the National bourse.
Brokers said the stock was hit by reports that foreign funds will not be able to buy the share because their holdings have reached the ceiling of 20 percent following the GDR issue.
"The big demand factor has now been removed," said Ramesh Damani, a member-broker at the BSE. "It'll have a negative impact on the prices in the near-term."
The GDRs were priced at $14.15 each on Thursday at a premium of 4.8 percent to the underlying stock, underwriter Lehman Brothers said in New York.
The $400 million issue, including $50 million greenshoe option, attracted commitments for nearly $900 million.
The size of the issue was finalised at $369.98 million because foreign portfolio holdings in SBI had reached the 20 percent ceiling.
